about: A search engine that works with existing Elasticsearch tools, built for AI agents to search code, docs and logs.

prs.title: Changing one cluster setting keeps the others
prs.broken: Saving one cluster-wide setting wiped every other setting saved before it. Settings sent in the nested style were stored but never used.
prs.changed: I made it merge each update into the saved settings, the way Elasticsearch does, and store every setting under one name form.
prs.matters: Earlier settings, like a disk or memory limit, stay in force when someone changes something else.

prs.title: Turning off the disk check lifts the full-disk block
prs.broken: When a disk got too full, writes were blocked. The standard setting to turn that check off was accepted but ignored, so the block stayed on.
prs.changed: I made the server read that setting, so turning the check off also lifts the block.
prs.matters: Users can unblock writes the same way they would in Elasticsearch.

prs.title: Date range searches now respect the time zone
prs.broken: A date range search ignored the time zone you gave it and read every date as UTC. Documents inside the real window were left out.
prs.changed: I made the search read dates in the given zone, including daylight saving changes, and round dates there too, the way Elasticsearch does.
prs.matters: Range searches with a time zone return the same documents as Elasticsearch.
